bug_semantics: Stored XSS: custom RSE attribute keys and values persisted by the API are interpolated into HTML and passed to jQuery append() on the RSE detail page, so a later viewer executes attacker HTML/JS in the WebUI origin.
flaw_origin: first-write of lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js in 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735: get_rse_attributes concatenated item and data[0][item] into an HTML string for $('#t_rse_attributes').append(). Later commits only extracted that concat into create_attributes_table; the 2026 fix replaced concat with .text() and element constructors.
evidence: GHSA-fq4f-4738-rqxm / CVE-2026-25736 (published; GHSA withdrawn_at null) describe stored XSS via custom RSE attributes rendered in WebUI. Pre-fix sink in lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js create_attributes_table used $('#t_rse_attributes').append($('' + item + '' + data[0][item] + '...')). git log --reverse -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js starts at 8f1a24a568331b10f9d8fb099ef233af340b7735 (2018-09-07, Hannes Hansen author and committer, single parent c77904c15e1958ad9f32e862b9e9714e48076434). git cat-file -p on that SHA: subject 'WebUI: added support for getting informations, creation and deletion of RSEs and attributes Fix #80'; no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot author. git cat-file -e PARENT:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/rse.js fails (path absent). BIC already had the HTML concat at the get_rse_attributes success handler. bf34d5206808923bc31091b0c5254a838e30e148 extracted the same concat into create_attributes_table (refactor, not first-write). fce81437e2e647a0da6e348167ea1df26db87c0c (fix(WebUI): fix XSS using jQuery.append) replaces concat with .text()/element constructors in rse.js and is an ancestor of tags 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1.
reasoning: Real stored XSS in rucio-webui RSE attribute rendering; advisory is not withdrawn. The first public commit that wrote the unescaped HTML concat of attacker-controlled attribute values is 8f1a24a5 (2018 human CERN author). Later extraction of create_attributes_table did not introduce the sink. BIC commit object has no AI authorship markers, so the causal origin is human.
